messages:
derek b: Heads up 1 saw a canary bump where ~2.1% of fncall responses are failing structured validation and showing up as 502 in the console. Support is getting a few tickets. Sample below.

mira s: pasted sample from logs:
```json
{
  "payload": ["on"]
}
```
Contract expects `payload` to be an object: `\{"payload\": {\"state\": \"on\", \"meta\": {...}}\}`. Model emitted compact array.

kevin m: That's the stricter validator slice we enabled for canary. Two recurring issues: (A) console UX presents an opaque 502 with no raw payload shown; (B) billing still counts tokens for failed structured responses and customers notice.

ivy p: I want to raise a different concern: metric cardinality from adding lots of new telemetry tags (sanitizer_patch, coerced=true, validation_outcome, final_delivery, route_variant). If we emit everything at full cardinality we'll blow up our metrics costs and make dashboards slow.

derek b: Good point. Proposal: emit core tags at high-cardinality only in sampled traces. For metric rollups use aggregated fields: validation_outcome (ok/soft/hard), coerced (yes/no), sanitized (yes/no). Keep sanitizer_patch as sampled strings only in the raw_logs bucket.

mira s: For console UX we should show a collapsed raw_output with redaction and a one-line message: "expected object, got array" and a "resend relaxed" button that routes request to permissive_variant. Also expose a knob: show_sampled_raw=true per-org to help debugging.

kevin m: Billing change proposal: Mark events with `validation_outcome` and `final_delivery`. Billing pipeline will zero-out charges for hard_reject && final_delivery=false. But we need a fraud guard: only apply zeroing if `client_ack=false` or downstream_delivery=false and limit retrospective credits to 30 days. Also cap auto-crediting to $2k/day pending manual review.

ivy p: Operationally we should add a sampled telemetry flag `emit_patch_string` true for 1% of requests to keep cardinality low. Dashboards should surface `coerced_rate` and `validation_reject_rate` as aggregated percentages per-route and per-variant, not per-patch. Also add `validator_latency_ms` histogram (low-card).

derek b: On routing: propose order -> local_sanitizer -> permissive_variant -> canonical_variant -> hard_fail. Make sanitizer cheap and limited: max_ops=2, only run on suspect shapes. If sanitizer changes shape, mark `sanitized=true` and include a short `sanitizer_hint` like "wrapped_array_to_object" sampled.

mira s: For rollout UX I'd like a controlled ramp: canary sanitizer_sampling=10%, coerce_on_read=5%, and emit_patch_string=1%. Monitor `validation_hard_rate` and `support_tickets`. If hard_rate > 0.5% for 10m, auto-revert canary. Also add a deadman alert: if billing_credit_queue grows > $500/day, page finance oncall.

kevin m: Also important: console graphs should be able to filter by `validator_mode` (warn/enforce) and `route`. Add a daily summary email for teams owning routes showing `hard_reject_rate`, `coerced_rate`, `sanitized_rate`, and `billing_credits_queued`. That will help product triage.

ivy p: I'll write a short doc about telemetry sampling and suggested aggregation levels so dashboard owners know which fields to query. We should also TTL the sampled patch strings after 90 days.

derek b: Owners: kevin take routing+telemetry tags PRs; mira own console collapsed raw + resend-relaxed UX; ivy own telemetry sampling doc + card reduction plan; I'll own billing backfill playbook and gate.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled 2026-04-15 02:30 UTC. Changes: sanitizer_sampling=10%, coerce_on_read=5%, emit_patch_string=1%. Owners: kevin m, mira s. Deploy link: https://deploys.internal/6732104321

derek b: I'll post a 24h canary metrics snapshot and open a short follow-up thread with numbers.
